title: The generating graph in the nerve of a free category
statement: Let $O$ be a small set and $Q$ a small directed graph on $O$, given by a set $Q(x,y)$ of edges for every $x,y\in O$. Loops, parallel edges and isolated vertices are allowed. Let $P(Q)$ be the small free category [def-nagata-category] with objects $O$, morphisms finite composable words of edges, empty words as identities and concatenation as composition. Write $NP(Q)$ for its ordinary simplicial nerve, whose $n$-simplices are strings of $n$ composable morphisms. Let $K(Q)\subseteq NP(Q)$ be the smallest simplicial subset [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] containing every vertex and the one-simplex of every single edge of $Q$. Then the inclusion $K(Q)\hookrightarrow NP(Q)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence in the realization sense of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. No nonemptiness or connectedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories (1980), Section 2.8 and Proposition 2.9 at k=1, printed p.271 (PDF p.5); Section 2.1 defines free categories. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: A nondegenerate simplex of the ordinary nerve is a string of nonidentity composable arrows. In the free category each such arrow is a nonempty word of edges. Concatenating the words gives a finite edge word w, and the cuts between successive arrows give a subset T of the positions between letters; conversely (w,T) reconstructs the simplex uniquely. The simplicial subset generated by vertices and single-edge 1-simplices therefore contains exactly the simplices with word length at most one, together with their faces and degeneracies. This is the elementary word-and-cuts description of K(Q).

source.place: Section 2.8, description of the simplices generated by the graph; word-and-cuts description supplied by the worker

proof.text: Filter by the total edge-word length L, starting with all vertices and the length-one part K(Q). For each L≥2, and then each r=0,…,L−2, attach simultaneously for every length-L composable edge word w and every S⊆{2,…,L−1} with |S|=r the simplex with cuts T={1}∪S. Its dimension is r+2. Use the horn Λ¹^{r+2}→Δ^{r+2}, as defined in the cited node. The missing d₁-face has cuts S. Every other inner face removes a cut of S and retains 1, so it belongs to an earlier r-stage; both outer faces delete a nonempty initial or terminal subword, so belong to an earlier L-stage. Thus the horn maps into the previous stage. The only nondegenerate simplices of Δ^{r+2} outside this horn are its top simplex and the interior of the missing face; their images have labels (w,{1}∪S) and (w,S), respectively. These labels are new and are distinct across attachments by unique factorization into edges. In any degree, a nerve simplex is uniquely its nonempty arrow words with empty words inserted at specified places. Therefore their degeneracies are also distinct and new. Pushouts of simplicial sets are computed degreewise, so the resulting pushout is exactly the simplicial subset obtained by adjoining these pairs. Repeated vertices of w may identify faces already in the horn, but cannot identify any of these new labels; the argument consequently permits loops and parallel edges. All indexing sets are small, and the successive finite r-stages for L=2,3,… form a countable cellular filtration.

source.place: Section 2.8 and Proposition 2.9 at k=1, printed p.271 (PDF p.5); agent-written word-and-cuts proof of the omitted combinatorial details, not a horn construction printed in the source

proof.text: Every nondegenerate simplex of length L≥2 occurs in this filtration: if its cut set contains 1 it is one of the attached simplices, and if it does not contain 1 it is the missing d₁-face of the attachment with the additional cut 1. Degenerate simplices are supplied automatically by the simplicial-subset closure. Thus the transfinite composite of the displayed pushouts is exactly the inclusion K(Q)↪NP(Q), including graphs with loops, parallel edges, isolated vertices, and the empty graph or empty vertex set.

source.place: Section 2.8 and Proposition 2.9 at k=1; exhaustion for the worker’s word-and-cuts filtration

proof.text: The cited Kan–Quillen model-structure statement says that trivial cofibrations are retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions. Hence the filtration map K(Q)→NP(Q) is a trivial cofibration, and therefore a weak homotopy equivalence in the realization sense specified there. No basepoint, component, finiteness, or connectedness hypothesis was used.
